correctness.rationale: For n=p^e Frobenius sends every nonconstant monomial to zero, so every substitution in the maximal ideal respects the exponent relations; invertible tangent matrices give automorphisms by nilpotent inverse-function/Nakayama and count of free higher coefficients. For n=h+1, the degree h+1 part of f^(h+1) forces every nonzero tangent generator to be on one axis, hence the tangent matrix monomial. Writing f=x_j u+b with b free of x_j, the lowest degree of nonzero b contributes uncancellable x_j^h b_s to f^(h+1), forcing b=0. Counting distinct elements of (x_j) with nonzero x_j coefficient gives the formula without unit-representative overcount. Independent direct full F2,d=2 enumerations return 24 and 2048 for n=2,3.
